raw_text:
Below is the full integrated 12-week muscle-gain program for your 26-year-old strict vegan recreational lifter with full gym access. It includes the three training phases (progression and exact weekly sessions), cardio, cheat-meal guidance, post-workout meal examples, high-protein breakfast options, protein powder recommendation, and Phase 3 intensity upgrades. Weekly structure, exercises, sets/reps, progression rules, nutrition notes (hitting 150 g protein/day), and recovery guidance are included so you can hand this directly to your client.

Client summary & assumptions
- 26-year-old female, strict vegan, recreational lifter (comfortable with barbell/dumbbell lifts).
- Goal: maximize muscle gain over 12 weeks.
- Nutrition target: 150 g protein/day from plant sources only.
- Training availability: 4 resistance sessions/week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B). Cardio 2–3x/week added.
- Full gym access.

Program overview (big picture)
- 12 weeks divided into 3 phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation & volume adaptation (RPE ~7).
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Hypertrophy emphasis — increased density and volume (RPE ~7.5–8.5).
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification / heavy emphasis + advanced techniques (RPE ~8–9; pushed intensity).
- Frequency: 4 weight sessions/week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B). Cardio scheduled mostly on non-heavy days.
- Weekly example schedule:
  - Mon: Upper A
  - Tue: Lower A (+ optional short LISS)
  - Wed: Cardio + mobility
  - Thu: Upper B
  - Fri: Lower B (+ optional short LISS)
  - Sat: LISS / active recovery (or cheat meal evening)
  - Sun: Rest

Warm-up & session format
- Warm-up: 8–12 min general + specific ramp sets for main lifts.
- Main compounds: 2–3 per session.
- Accessories: 3–5 per session.
- Tempo: controlled eccentrics (2–3s) unless specified (some eccentrics up to 4–5s in Phase 3).
- Rest: 2–3 min for heavy compounds; 60–90s for accessories; cluster/rest-pause short rests as specified.
- Progression: add reps then load (1–2 reps up to top of range then +2.5–5%); track weekly. Auto-regulate using RPE and bar speed.

Cardio plan (integrated)
- Phase 1 (Wks 1–4): 2–3 sessions/week, 60–90 min total. LISS 30–40 min + 1 MISS 20–30 min + optional 10–15 min post-lift LISS.
- Phase 2 (Wks 5–8): 2–3 sessions/week, 75–105 min total. LISS/MISS + one short HIIT (8–10 x 20s work/40s rest). Avoid heavy lift interference.
- Phase 3 (Wks 9–12): 2–3 sessions/week, 75–150 min depending on intensity. MISS 30–40 min + interval or longer LISS session on weekend. No HIIT within 48 hrs of heavy lower sessions.
- Keep cardio after lifting short and low intensity if same day.

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundation & volume adaptation
Goal: Build work capacity, technique, baseline volume. Moderate loads.

Weeks 1–2 (repeat Week 1 with small progressions)
Week 1
- Upper A (Mon)
  1. Barbell bench press – 4 x 8 (2/0/1) Rest 90–120s
  2. Pull-ups (assisted/weighted) – 4 x 6–8 Rest 90–120s
  3. Seated DB shoulder press – 3 x 10 Rest 75–90s
  4. Incline DB or chest-supported row – 3 x 10 Rest 75–90s
  5. Cable triceps pushdown – 3 x 12 Rest 60–75s
  6. DB hammer curls – 3 x 12 Rest 60–75s

- Lower A (Tue)
  1. Back squat – 4 x 8 Rest 2–3 min
  2. Romanian deadlift – 3 x 8–10 Rest 2 min
  3. Bulgarian split squat – 3 x 10/leg Rest 90s
  4. Leg curl – 3 x 12 Rest 60–75s
  5. Standing calf raises – 4 x 12–15 Rest 45–60s
  6. Plank – 3 x 45s

- Upper B (Thu)
  1. Overhead press (barbell) – 4 x 8 Rest 90–120s
  2. Barbell or T-bar row – 4 x 8 Rest 90–120s
  3. DB incline press – 3 x 10 Rest 75–90s
  4. Face pulls – 3 x 15 Rest 60s
  5. Lateral raises – 3 x 12 Rest 60–75s
  6. EZ-bar curls – 3 x 12 Rest 60–75s

- Lower B (Fri)
  1. Deadlift (RDL or conventional) – 4 x 6–8 Rest 2–3 min
  2. Front squat or goblet squat – 3 x 8–10 Rest 2 min
  3. Hip thrust – 3 x 10 Rest 90s
  4. Leg press – 3 x 12 Rest 90s
  5. Seated calf raises – 4 x 12–15 Rest 45–60s
  6. Hanging leg raises – 3 x 10–12

Week 2: add 2.5–5% load or 1–2 reps on main lifts if all sets completed.

Weeks 3–4
- Adjust main compounds to 4 x 6–8 and keep accessories 3–4 x 8–12.
- Add one unilateral upper accessory each upper session.
- Week 4: optional autoregulated deload if fatigued (reduce volume ~20%).

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Focused hypertrophy
Goal: Increase density, time under tension, and total weekly volume.

Week 5 (example)
- Upper A (Mon)
  1. Barbell bench – 5 x 6–8
  2. Weighted pull-ups/lat pulldown – 4 x 8
  3. Seated DB press – 4 x 8–10
  4. Chest-supported row – 4 x 8–10
  5. Incline cable fly – 3 x 12–15
  6. Overhead triceps ext – 3 x 10–12

- Lower A (Tue)
  1. Back squat – work-up then 4 x 6–8
  2. RDL – 4 x 8
  3. Walking lunges – 3 x 12 steps/leg
  4. Glute-ham / Nordic curl – 3 x 8–10
  5. Calf raises – 4 x 12–15
  6. Pallof press – 3 x 30s/side

- Upper B (Thu)
  1. Incline press – 4 x 8
  2. Bent-over row – 4 x 8
  3. DB lateral raises (slow) – 4 x 12
  4. Seated cable row – 3 x 10–12
  5. Face pulls – 3 x 15
  6. Barbell curls – 3 x 10–12

- Lower B (Fri)
  1. Deadlift – 4 x 5–6
  2. Front squat – 4 x 6–8
  3. Hip thrust – 4 x 8–10
  4. Bulgarian split squat – 3 x 10/leg
  5. Hamstring curl – 3 x 12–15
  6. Russian twists – 3 x 20 total

Weeks 6–7: progress load/reps. Add occasional drop-sets on accessories.

Week 8: include an intensity set (AMRAP) on a main lift or insert an autoregulated lighter week as needed.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Intensification with pushed intensity (revised)
Goal: Push intensity with heavy compounds, clusters, rest-pause, and peak strength work while preserving hypertrophy volume via back-off sets. Monitor recovery closely.

Weekly structure (revised)
- Mon: Upper A (HEAVY strength)
- Tue: Lower A (volume + heavy accents)
- Wed: Cardio/mobility (LISS/MISS)
- Thu: Upper B (volume + intensity techniques)
- Fri: Lower B (HEAVY deadlift/squat focus)
- Sat: LISS / active recovery and optional cheat meal evening
- Sun: Rest

Week 9 (example)
- Upper A (Mon) — HEAVY
  1. Barbell bench — 3 x 5 @ ~80–85% + 3 back-off sets 8–10 @ 65–70%
  2. Weighted pull-ups — 5 x 4–6
  3. Incline DB press — 3 x 8 (last set rest-pause)
  4. Chest-supported row — 4 x 6–8
  5. Triceps OH ext superset face pulls — 3 x 8–10 + 3 x 15
  6. Hammer curls — 3 x 8–10

- Lower A (Tue) — VOLUME + HEAVY ACCENTS
  1. Back squat — 5 sets mixing 5/5/5/3/3 with last heavy sets RPE 8–9
  2. RDL — 4 x 6 (3s eccentric)
  3. Bulgarian split — 3 x 8/leg (last set dropset)
  4. Hip thrust — 4 x 6–8 (pause)
  5. Leg curl — 3 x 12 (rest-pause last set)
  6. Ab wheel — 3 x 10

- Upper B (Thu) — VOLUME/INTENSITY
  1. Overhead press — 5 x 5 heavy
  2. Barbell row — 5 x 5–6 heavy
  3. Flat DB press — 3 x 8 slow ecc
  4. Single-arm cable row — 3 x 10–12
  5. Lateral raises — 4 x 12 (last set dropset)
  6. EZ-bar curls — 3 x 10 + 1 AMRAP

- Lower B (Fri) — HEAVY
  1. Deadlift — heavy doubles/triples (e.g., 3–5 sets heavy) Rest 3–4 min
  2. Front squat — 4 x 5 heavy
  3. Single-leg hip thrust — 3 x 8–10/leg
  4. Leg press — 3 x 10 (dropset last)
  5. Calf complex — 4 x 12
  6. Hanging leg raises — 3 x 12

Week 10
- Introduce cluster sets for bench or deadlift (e.g., 5 x 3 @ 85% with 15–20s rest).
- Use rest-pause on one accessory per upper session.
- Keep accessory volume high enough for hypertrophy.

Week 11 (peak heavy)
- Work up to heavier singles/doubles at RPE ~9. Maintain back-off hypertrophy sets after heavy work.
- Limit total top heavy sets to avoid overreaching.

Week 12 (tapered consolidation)
- Reduce accessory volume by ~20–30% but maintain heavy top-set intensity (stop 1–2 reps shy of failure).
- Focus on mobility, sleep, and nutrition.

Advanced techniques (application & limits)
- Cluster sets: 1 lift/week (bench or dead) use 4–6 cluster sets.
- Rest-pause: limit to 1–2 accessories per session.
- Drop sets: on isolation movements only (1 drop/set).
- Eccentric overload (3–5s negatives): use on 1–2 sets/week max.
- AMRAPs: occasionally; stop 1–2 reps short of failure if nervous about CNS fatigue.

Nutrition: hitting 150 g protein/day (plant-based)
Calorie guidance
- Begin with maintenance + 250–350 kcal for muscle gain; adjust based on weight change (if unknown, estimate ~18–20 kcal/kg bodyweight).
- Protein: 150 g/day target (distribute over 4–6 meals).
- Fat: ~20–30% of calories.
- Carbs: fill remaining calories to support training.

Daily protein distribution (example)
- Breakfast: 30–45 g
- Mid-morning snack/post-workout shake: 25–40 g
- Lunch: 25–35 g
- Afternoon snack: 10–20 g
- Dinner: 25–35 g
- Late snack or shake if needed: 15–25 g

Key vegan protein sources & supplements
- High-protein foods: tempeh, tofu, seitan (if tolerated), edamame, lentils, chickpeas, black beans, peas, quinoa, hemp seeds, nutritional yeast.
- Protein powder: recommend soy isolate (if tolerated) or a pea+rice/multi-plant blend with ≥20–25 g protein/scoop and good leucine (~2.5–3 g if listed). Third-party tested brands preferred. Add creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day.
- Supplements: B12 (daily), vitamin D (as needed), algae-based omega-3, iron if labs low.

Protein powder recommendation (summary)
- If soy tolerated: soy protein isolate for completeness and leucine content.
- If soy avoided: pea protein isolate blended with rice or multi-plant athlete blends (pea+rice, pea+hemp+quinoa).

Week 11 (peak heavy intensity)
- Schedule maximal heavy work while avoiding true 1RM testing:
  - Attempt heavier singles/doubles on main lifts (bench, squat, deadlift, press) within RPE 9.

Advanced intensity techniques (how to use them safely)
- Cluster sets: Break a heavy set into multiple short-rest mini-sets (e.g., 5x3 with 15–30s rest). Allows greater heavy rep quality. Use only on main lifts and limit total volume.
- Rest-pause: Do a near-failure set, rest 10–20s, do more mini-sets to squeeze extra reps. Use on 1–2 accessories per session.
- Drop sets: Useful on isolation movements; perform one drop per exercise, avoid overusing.
- Tempo eccentrics: 3–5s slow negatives on 1–2 sets weekly to increase time under tension. Use conservative loads.
- AMRAP top sets: Occasionally do an AMRAP set but stop 1–2 reps shy of failure to avoid excessive CNS fatigue.
- Clustered heavy doubles/singles for neural drive but limit frequency to avoid CNS overreach.

- Phase 3 (Wks 9–12): 2–3 sessions/week, 75–150 min depending on intensity. MISS 30–40 min + interval or longer LISS session on weekend. No HIIT within 48 hrs of heavy lower sessions.
- Keep cardio after lifting short and low intensity if same day.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Intensification with pushed intensity (revised)
Goal: Push intensity with heavy compounds, clusters, rest-pause, and peak strength work while preserving hypertrophy volume via back-off sets. Monitor recovery closely.

- Mon: Upper A (HEAVY strength)
- Tue: Lower A (volume + heavy accents)
- Wed: Cardio/mobility (LISS/MISS)
- Thu: Upper B (volume + intensity techniques)
- Fri: Lower B (HEAVY deadlift/squat focus)

  5. Calf complex — 4 x 12

Week 10
- Introduce cluster sets for bench or deadlift (e.g., 5 x 3 @ 85% with 15–20s rest).
- Use rest-pause on one accessory per upper session.
- Keep accessory volume high enough for hypertrophy.

Week 11 (peak heavy)
- Work up to heavier singles/doubles at RPE ~9. Maintain back-off hypertrophy sets after heavy work.
- Limit total top heavy sets to avoid overreaching.

Week 12 (tapered consolidation)
- Reduce accessory volume by ~20–30% but maintain heavy top-set intensity (stop 1–2 reps shy of failure).
- Focus on mobility, sleep, and nutrition.

Advanced techniques (application & limits)
- Cluster sets: 1 lift/week (bench or dead) use 4–6 cluster sets.
- Rest-pause: limit to 1–2 accessories per session.
- Drop sets: on isolation movements only (1 drop/set).
- Eccentric overload (3–5s negatives): use on 1–2 sets/week max.
- AMRAPs: occasionally; stop 1–2 reps short of failure if nervous about CNS fatigue.

Nutrition: hitting 150 g protein/day (plant-based)
Calorie guidance
- Begin with maintenance + 250–350 kcal for muscle gain; adjust based on weight change (if unknown, estimate ~18–20 kcal/kg bodyweight).
- Protein: 150 g/day target (distribute over 4–6 meals).
- Fat: ~20–30% of calories.
- Carbs: fill remaining calories to support training.

Daily protein distribution (example)
- Breakfast: 30–45 g
- Mid-morning snack/post-workout shake: 25–40 g
- Lunch: 25–35 g
- Afternoon snack: 10–20 g
- Dinner: 25–35 g
- Late snack or shake if needed: 15–25 g

Key vegan protein sources & supplements
- High-protein foods: tempeh, tofu, seitan (if tolerated), edamame, lentils, chickpeas, black beans, peas, quinoa, hemp seeds, nutritional yeast.
- Protein powder: recommend soy isolate (if tolerated) or a pea+rice/multi-plant blend with ≥20–25 g protein/scoop and good leucine (~2.5–3 g if listed). Third-party tested brands preferred. Add creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day.
- Supplements: B12 (daily), vitamin D (as needed), algae-based omega-3, iron if labs low.

Protein powder recommendation (summary)
- If soy tolerated: soy protein isolate for completeness and leucine content.
- If soy avoided: pea protein isolate blended with rice or multi-plant athlete blends (pea+rice, pea+hemp+quinoa).
- Criteria: ≥20 g protein/scoop, minimal fillers, third-party tested (NSF/Informed Sport), good taste/mixability.
- Example brands to consider: Naked Pea, Vega Sport, Orgain, Sunwarrior, Myprotein Vegan Blend (choose local availability).

Cheat meal guidance (one meal/week)
- One meal per week (Saturday evening recommended) to satisfy cravings and social needs.
- Keep it a single meal (not a full binge day). Plan other meals that day to be protein-rich to stay near 100–150 g overall; ideally still hit 150 g with a corrective shake if necessary.
- Vegan cheat examples: vegan burger + fries, vegan pizza, loaded nachos/burrito, vegan “chicken” tenders, dessert (vegan brownies + ice cream).
- If cheat low in protein, add a post-cheat protein shake (20–30 g) to protect gains.

Recovery & injury-prevention
- Sleep 7–9 hours/night (prefer 8+ on heavy weeks).
- Mobility: thoracic spine, shoulders, hip flexors, posterior chain 2–3x/week.
- Foam roll 1–3x/week.
- Warm-up properly and use progressive ramp sets before heavy lifts. Use a spotter or safety pins for heavy bench/squat.
- Auto-regulate: if two consecutive sessions show stalled performance, insert a deload or scale intensity back.

Monitoring & progression rules
- Track working set weights, reps, RPE weekly. Aim to increase reps then weight (small increments: 1–2 reps then +2.5–5%).
- Adjust calories if no weight gain after 2–3 weeks: +200–300 kcal/day. If gaining too fast (>0.8–1% bodyweight/month), reduce surplus.
- If performance/energy drops, reduce HIIT, lower accessory volume, increase carbs and sleep.

Safety notes
- If gluten-intolerant, avoid seitan and substitute tempeh/soy/pea-based proteins.
- Monitor iron/B12/D levels with bloodwork and supplement appropriately.
- For joint pain, reduce load or swap to machine or unilateral variations.
